It is a specific, substantive architecture/scope concern grounded in cited diff lines — future or existing consumers that rebuild evt from booking.destinationCalendar (the exact pattern repeated in bookingReminder, webhooks, confirm/editLocation handlers in this diff) will see only one calendar for collective bookings — but the finding describes an under-representation risk, not a verified defect introduced here.

judged_text: The booking record connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` even when the diff's new collective flow populates several destination calendars and creates calendar events for all of them. For collective bookings, the persisted Booking.destinationCalendar relation under-represents the actual destinations (only the organizer/eventType's is linked); any consumer that reconstructs evt from booking.destinationCalendar — the pattern this diff itself repeats in bookingReminder, payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/requestReschedule handlers — sees only the first calendar, so future flows built on that relation will operate on one member's calendar while events exist on several.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a mismatch between the new multi-destination runtime model and what gets persisted on the Booking. In `handleNewBooking.ts`, collective/team logic can append multiple calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` to create events for each. However, the Booking write still only connects a single destination calendar via `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`, so the Booking’s `destinationCalendar` relation cannot represent all destinations used for event creation. The diff also continues to reconstruct `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (wrapped into a single-element array) in multiple places (e.g., bookingReminder, payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/requestReschedule), which would only ever carry that single persisted destination. While the diff doesn’t conclusively prove an immediate broken flow (updates/deletes now primarily use calendar references), it is a concrete, diff-grounded inconsistency that can cause future/adjacent logic that relies on `booking.destinationCalendar` to under-operate (only the first calendar) despite events having been created on multiple calendars.
